Zeeland Tide Reconstruction (5-min model)

CUTS+ learns one causal graph over 77 Zeeland water-level gauges, then a single shared network uses it to predict every gauge's next 5-minute reading from the others. These are those one-step-ahead predictions replayed against the real readings on three sessions the model never trained on (resampled onto a 5-minute grid - compare against zeeland_tide_reconstruction.html's 15-minute/sparsity_fine_08 model for the same idea at a coarser sampling rate).

config: zeeland_flood_eval_5min λ_s = 0.08 fixed, no anneal region: Zeeland held-out score session

Prediction is one-step-ahead (5 min) using the trained fitting network + the final discovered graph, not a multi-step forecast — the model sees the real previous reading at every step. Reading this as a forecast would understate the error; it answers "does the learned graph explain the next 5-minute reading given the current one," which is what CUTS+ optimizes.

Actual/predicted/RMSE are derived directly (no model forward pass) from zeeland_flood_eval_5min/models's saved z-scores, residual median/std and the dataset's channel normalization stats - same flood-aware-split run compared against the 15-min run (cuts_plus_prototype/run_zeeland_flood_eval_5min.sh), same λ_s = 0.08 fixed / no anneal hyperparameters as sparsity_fine_08.
